# Average Cost for 1800 GOT JUNK in Seattle  

If you’ve typed “average cost for 1800 GOT JUNK in Seattle” into Google, you’re probably facing a pile of unwanted items and wondering how much it will hurt your wallet. In this guide we break down exactly what you can expect to pay, why prices vary, how 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? stacks up against local competitors, and what hidden fees to watch out for. By the end you’ll have a **clear, data‑driven budget** and the confidence to choose the right service for your situation.  

---

## 1. How 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? Calculates Its Prices in Seattle  

### 1.1 Base Truck Load Fees  

1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? uses a **per‑truck‑load pricing model** rather than a per‑pound or per‑item charge. In Seattle the standard rates for a single 10‑yard truck (the most common size) range from **$149 to $199**. The exact amount depends on:  

- **Location** – Central Seattle ZIP codes (98101, 98109) are typically $10‑$20 higher than outlying neighborhoods (e.g., Shoreline, Burien) due to traffic and permit costs.  
- **Season** – Summer months (June–August) see a 5‑10 % price bump because demand spikes for renovation clean‑outs.  
- **Load Volume** – If the crew can fit the junk into one truck, you pay the base fee. Two partially‑filled trucks trigger the second‑truck surcharge, usually **$100‑$130**.  

### 1.2 Additional Services That Add Cost  

| Service | Typical Extra Charge (Seattle) | When It Applies |
|---------|-------------------------------|-----------------|
| **Heavy‑Item Lifting** (pianos, hot‑tubs) | **+$50‑$80** | Items over 300 lb that need extra manpower |
| **Hazardous Waste** (asbestos, chemicals) | **+$75‑$120** | Must be disposed at a certified facility |
| **Staircase/ Elevator Access** | **+$30‑$50** | When crews must navigate stairs or limited elevators |
| **Same‑Day Service** | **+$30‑$70** | For last‑minute pickups (usually within 24 hrs) |

These add‑ons are **optional**; the company will always ask for approval before proceeding.

### 1.3 Real‑World Example: Two‑Bedroom Apartment Clean‑Out  

*Scenario*: A renter in Capitol Hill moves out, leaving a sofa, mattress, TV, a box of books, and a broken coffee table. The crew estimates the load will fill **one 10‑yard truck**.  

- Base fee: **$169** (average Seattle rate)  
- No heavy items, no stairs (elevator access is free)  
- Total: **$169**  

If the same renter had a piano and needed the crew to carry it down three flights of stairs, the final bill could climb to **$239** (adding a $70 heavy‑item fee and a $30 stair surcharge).  

---  

## 2. Comparing 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? With Local Seattle Alternatives  

### 2.1 Dumpster Rental vs. Full‑Service Junk Removal  

| Feature | 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? | Typical Seattle Dumpster Rental |
|---------|----------------|---------------------------------|
| **Pricing Model** | Per truck load (all‑in) | Daily or weekly flat fee + per‑ton disposal |
| **Labor** | Crew loads and hauls | You load the dumpster yourself |
| **Time Commitment** | 1‑2 hrs (crew does everything) | 1‑3 days to fill, plus pickup time |
| **Best For** | Small‑to‑medium residential clean‑outs | Large remodels, construction sites |

**Pros of 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK?**: No lifting on your part, transparent all‑in price, quick turnaround.  
**Cons**: Slightly higher price for small loads because you pay for the whole truck even if it’s half empty.  

**Dumpster rental** can be cheaper if you have **lots of bulk material** (e.g., demolition debris) and are willing to load it yourself. A 20‑yard roll‑off in Seattle averages **$350‑$420 per week**, plus a disposal fee of **$55‑$70 per ton**.  

### 2.2 Local “Junk Haulers” – The Hybrid Option  

Seattle has a vibrant market of independent junk haulers who often price by **cubic yard** or **per‑item**. Examples include “Seattle Junk Guys” and “Green Earth Disposal.” Their typical rates:  

- **$120‑$150** for the first 8 cubic yards (roughly a 10‑yard truck)  
- **$30‑$45** per additional cubic yard  
- **$45‑$70** per heavy item (piano, safe)  

These firms may offer **discounts for repeat customers** or **non‑profit projects**, but they sometimes lack the **insurance coverage** that 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? guarantees (their crews are fully insured for up to **$2 million**).  

### 2.3 When to Choose One Over the Other  

| Situation | Recommended Service |
|-----------|----------------------|
| **One‑off apartment move** | 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? (quick, no labor) |
| **Full‑house renovation** (10+ tons) | Dumpster rental (lower per‑ton cost) |
| **Small yard clean‑up** (few bulky items) | Local junk hauler (cheapest for tiny loads) |
| **Eco‑conscious disposal** (must recycle) | Any service that provides a **recycling report**; 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? publishes an annual “diversion rate” of **> 85 %** from landfill. |

---  

## 3. Hidden Costs & Common Misconceptions  

### 3.1 “Free Estimates” Are Not Always Free  

Most Seattle junk removal companies, including 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK?, advertise a **free on‑site estimate**. In practice:  

- **Phone quotes** are usually rough ranges.  
- The **final price** can shift once the crew sees the actual volume and any hard‑to‑move items.  

If you want an exact figure, request a **written estimate** that lists each potential surcharge.  

### 3.2 “We Take Anything” – What Actually Gets Rejected  

Both 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? and local haulers **refuse hazardous waste** that requires special handling (e.g., paint cans, batteries, propane tanks). If you try to include these, expect an **additional $100‑$200** for proper disposal, or better yet, separate them beforehand.  

### 3.3 “All‑Inclusive” Does Not Mean “All‑Eco”.  

While 1‑800‑GOT‑JUNK? boasts a high diversion rate, some items are **landfilled** because recycling is impractical (e.g., broken concrete). If your priority is **maximal recycling**, ask the crew for a **post‑service waste breakdown**.
